entries.content: X. Artru, 'String Model with Baryons: Topology, Classical Motion', Nucl. Phys. B 85, 442-460 (1975). Introduces the junction as the object needed to accommodate baryons in string models: a combination of three strings stretched between the three quarks, meeting at a single point. This is the topological origin of the Y-configuration; the paper treats its topology and classical motion. Confirms digest ref [3] as the founding junction paper.

G.C. Rossi and G. Veneziano, 'A possible description of baryon dynamics in dual and gauge theories', Nucl. Phys. B 123 (3), 507-545 (1977). In dual/gauge theory language the baryon junction is the Y-shaped gluonic topology connecting the three valence quarks; local gauge invariance requires the string operators joining at a junction, making the junction-plus-quarks configuration the gauge-invariant baryon operator carrying B = 1. This is the paper that ties baryon number to the junction as a matter of gauge invariance, and the origin of the junction-based 'baryonium' proposal.

G. Rossi, G. Veneziano, 'The string-junction picture of multiquark states: an update', JHEP 06 (2016) 041, arXiv:1603.05830. Recalls and updates the ~40-year-old junction proposal as a necessary complement to quark-only hadron classification. Key claim: hadrons containing junctions are 'mesophobic' — unusually narrow if they lie below the threshold for decaying into as many baryons as their total junction count (2 junctions for a junction tetraquark, 3 for a pentaquark). They present experimental support: narrow multiquark candidates typically sit below the relevant baryonic thresholds and well above mesonic ones. This is the modern statement of the junction-counting selection rule GUM's tetraquark-kill logic parallels.

D. Kharzeev, Phys. Lett. B 378, 238 (1996), nucl-th/9602027, DOI 10.1016/0370-2693(96)00435-2 (received 15 Mar 1996, CERN Theory/Bielefeld). Thesis: contrary to accepted belief, traces of baryon number in high-energy processes reside in non-perturbative gluon-field configurations, not valence quarks. Argument: local gauge invariance of the proton wave function means the baryon is string operators acting on quark fields; B is carried by the non-perturbative gluon configuration at the string junction. Prediction: substantial baryon asymmetry at central rapidity in ultra-relativistic AA collisions — junctions (unlike hard valence quarks) are low-x/slow and can be stopped by the projectile's soft parton field; stopping cross section falls only exponentially (slowly) in rapidity loss, with the slope set by the junction Regge intercept. This is the source of the exp(-alpha_B * Delta-y) transport law used by STAR.

As relayed by the STAR methodology papers (arXiv:2205.05685 -> EPJC 84 (2024) and the EIC study arXiv:2408.07131): the rapidity slope of transported net baryons is alpha_J = 2 - alpha_0^J - alpha_P(0) = 0.42 for SINGLE-junction stopping (junction + Pomeron exchange), and alpha_J = 2 - 2*alpha_0^J = 1 for DOUBLE-junction (J+J) stopping, using the junction trajectory intercept alpha_0^J ~ 0.5 and Pomeron intercept alpha_P(0) = 1.08 (alpha_P(0) - 1 = 0.08). Check: 2 - 0.5 - 1.08 = 0.42; 2 - 2(0.5) = 1. This pins the digest's window 0.42 < alpha_B < 1 and identifies the two-parameter provenance (junction intercept 1/2; soft-Pomeron 1.08). A related non-junction/valence decomposition (arXiv:2504.09826) quotes intercepts -0.5, 0, +0.5 for configurations taking 2, 1, 0 valence quarks from the proton respectively.

entries.content: T. Csorgo, M. Gyulassy, D. Kharzeev, 'Buckyballs and gluon junction networks on the femtometre scale', J. Phys. G 30, L17-L25 (2004), arXiv:hep-ph/0112066 (submitted Dec 2001; companion earlier proceedings 'Buckyballs of QCD: gluon junction networks', hep-ph/0102282). States constructed: closed gluon-field cages/networks of baryon junctions and anti-junctions — femtometer cousins of C60/C70 fullerenes. The most symmetric closed polyhedra (J-balls) carry 'magic numbers' of 8, 24, 48, and 120 junctions and ZERO net baryon number; tubes, prisms, tori and other topologies also constructible. The SIMPLEST quarkless bound state is the 'baryonium' J-ball formed by connecting one junction with one anti-junction (the J-Jbar dumbbell — GUM's minimal three-tube case), which despite being pure glue with B=0 'has a large coupling to baryon wave functions'. The paper gives a SEMI-CLASSICAL ESTIMATE of the expected mass range of QCD buckyballs and estimates relative binding energies plus production conditions/signatures — but the numerical GeV values could not be pinned from any accessible snippet (see unverified).

entries.topic: Lattice Y-law: Takahashi et al. PRL 86 (2001)
entries.content: T.T. Takahashi, H. Matsufuru, Y. Nemoto, H. Suganuma, 'Three-Quark Potential in SU(3) Lattice QCD', Phys. Rev. Lett. 86, 18-21 (2001). 12^3 x 24 lattice at beta = 5.7; ground-state 3Q potential extracted from the 3Q Wilson loop with smearing. Result: V_3Q is well described by constant + two-body Coulomb + three-body LINEAR confinement term sigma_3Q * L_min, where L_min is the minimal total flux-tube length linking the three quarks (the Y/Steiner configuration). With the Y-ansatz, the extracted 3Q string tension nearly coincides with the quark-antiquark string tension sigma_QQbar — supporting the Y-type flux-tube (genuine junction) picture over the Delta ansatz.

entries.topic: Lattice Y-law: Suganuma et al. AIP Conf. Proc. 756 (2005)
entries.content: H. Suganuma, T.T. Takahashi, F. Okiharu, H. Ichie, 'Lattice QCD Study for the Interquark Force in Three-Quark and Multi-Quark Systems', AIP Conf. Proc. 756, 123-132 (2005). Reports that the static ground-state 3Q potential is described by Coulomb plus Y-type linear potential (Y-ansatz) at the 1%-deviation level, and extends the analysis to multi-quark (4Q, 5Q) systems — the quantitative precision statement banked by GUM's Y-law structural consistency.

entries.topic: Lattice Y-law: Bissey et al. PRD 76, 114512 (2007)
entries.content: F. Bissey, F-G. Cao, A.R. Kitson, A.I. Signal (Massey) with D.B. Leinweber, B.G. Lasscock, A.G. Williams (Adelaide), 'Gluon flux-tube distribution and linear confinement in baryons', Phys. Rev. D 76, 114512 (2007), hep-lat/0606016. Direct visualization of gluon flux distribution in static baryons: studied 11 L-shaped and 8 T- and Y-shaped quark arrangements; at LARGE separations Y-shape flux-tube formation is observed and T-shaped arrangements RELAX toward Y-shaped topology; NO evidence for Delta-shaped (empty-triangle) flux distribution. Complements the potential-fit evidence with flux-density evidence for a genuine central junction.

'The Mass of the Baryon Junction: a lattice computation in 2+1 dimensions' (arXiv:2508.00608): systematic lattice study of a three-string baryonic configuration in 3D SU(3) Yang-Mills, extracting the junction mass M via NLO Effective String Theory expressions: M/sqrt(sigma) = 0.1355(36). This is the first direct quantification of the junction-energy term found in this sweep — the junction contributes a small POSITIVE point-mass correction on top of the Y-law string lengths (2+1D caveat). Theory frame: Komargodski-Zhong, 'The Baryon Junction and String Interactions', Phys. Rev. D 110, 056018 (2024), arXiv:2405.12005 — the junction EFT has ONE new parameter (the junction mass) controlling leading finite-size corrections; via open-closed duality junction properties map to closed-string interaction vertices in Yang-Mills; surprising selection rules in 3+1D; perturbative stability + weak string coupling constrain the junction mass. Follow-up: 'Baryon Junction and String Interactions: Part II' (arXiv:2602.17771).

J.R. Christiansen, P.Z. Skands, 'String formation beyond leading colour', JHEP 08 (2015) 003, arXiv:1505.01681. New hadronisation model where colour correlations beyond leading-N_C influence string formation: SU(3) multiplet structure combined with string-length (potential-energy) minimisation decides which partons form strings, explicitly allowing 'baryonic' configurations — two or three string pieces colour-connected to a junction plus anti-junction system, each producing at least one (anti)baryon. In e+e- the effects are small (colour- and kinematics-suppressed); in pp, multi-parton interactions multiply subleading connections, counteracting the naive 1/N_C^2 suppression, and length-reducing reconnections are kinematically favoured. Implemented in PYTHIA 8; reproduces <pT>(n_ch) and baryon rates. The 'CR Mode 2' cited by STAR (which drives their junction-like ratio to 0.99 +/- 0.03): modes 0/2/3 differ in time-dilation/causality constraints — mode 2 requires ALL dipoles involved in a reconnection to be causally connected, with time dilation computed from the boost factor of the final-state dipole mass; mode 2 also reproduces enhanced charm-baryon/charm-meson ratios.

L. Lonnblad, H. Shah, 'Baryon correlations in Pythia', Eur. Phys. J. C 83, 1105 (2023), arXiv:2309.01557. Investigates angular correlations between baryon pairs in PYTHIA 8: how colour-reconnection models (including the QCD-based junction-forming CR) and hadronization mechanisms shape baryon-baryon and baryon-antibaryon correlations; compares to ALICE pp baryon angular-correlation data (which the default and junction models struggle to describe); studies the effect of gluons on baryon production in Lund string fragmentation and proposes a hypothesis suppressing baryons produced in gluon jets. Relevant to GUM as the state-of-the-art phenomenological test bed for junction-induced baryon correlations.

(1) Frenklakh-Kharzeev et al., 'Baryon-number-flavor separation in the topological expansion of QCD', JHEP 07 (2024) 262, arXiv:2405.04569: gauge invariance dictates junctions in baryon wave functions; predicts TWO DEGENERATE junction-antijunction GLUEBALL Regge trajectories of OPPOSITE C-parity with intercept close to 1/2 — i.e., the J-Jbar 'baryonium glueball' is organized into Regge trajectories (masses follow from the trajectory with standard slope, not printed in accessible snippets); also predicts baryon-number/flavor flow separation, in reasonable agreement with STAR and ALICE stopping data. (2) Komargodski-Zhong PRD 110, 056018 (2024) + Part II (arXiv:2602.17771) + lattice M/sqrt(sigma)=0.1355(36) (arXiv:2508.00608) give the junction a well-defined mass parameter in effective string theory. (3) Older thread: 'String junction as a baryonic constituent' (PLB 1995) and 'Baryonium, tetra-quark state and glue-ball in large N_c QCD' (arXiv:0710.4185) treat junction-antijunction baryonium in large-N. No accessible source printed an explicit GeV mass for the minimal J-Jbar dumbbell.

entries.topic: Companion methodology paper and post-2024 reactions
entries.content: Companion: Lewis et al. (incl. Kharzeev, Xu et al.), 'Search for baryon junctions in photonuclear processes and isobar collisions at RHIC', Eur. Phys. J. C 84 (2024), arXiv:2205.05685 — pre-registers the isobar B/DeltaQ and photonuclear exp(-alpha_B Delta-y) tests, quoting the 0.42-1 Regge window and reporting an extracted alpha_B = 0.61 +/- 0.03 from existing net-proton data ('qualitatively consistent' with junctions). entries.content: The STAR paper 'Tracking the baryon number with nuclear collisions' was published in SCIENCE, DOI 10.1126/science.ads5962, appearing 2026-08-13 (i.e., three days before today's date; submitted to arXiv 2024-08-27 — a ~2-year review). Corroborated independently by: the science.org DOI page title in search results; BNL Newsroom release 'Gluons May Play Central Role in Baryon Number Conservation' (bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=122692), which states the paper 'appeared in Science on August 13, 2026' and notes RHIC 'operated from 2000 to early 2026'; EurekAlert release 1139404 'Gluons carry a proton's baryon number'; Sci.News, ScienceAlert, Science News, The Debrief, Newswise, Mirage News, and a Rice University release. An accompanying SCIENCE PERSPECTIVE by Wenliang Li frames the result but cautions that the measurements 'do not provide a direct, tightly controlled measurement of the underlying mechanism.' Volume/issue/page numbers were not recoverable from snippets (DOI only).

Confirmed: N. Lewis et al., 'Search for baryon junctions in photonuclear processes and isobar collisions at RHIC', Eur. Phys. J. C 84, 590 (2024), DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12834-2, arXiv:2205.05685 (v1 title was 'Testing the baryon-junction conjecture in photonuclear processes and isobar collisions at RHIC' — title changed at publication; v3 is the published version). This is the paper that proposed the exponential exp(-alpha_B * dy) net-baryon signature and the isobar B/DeltaQ double-ratio observable later executed in the Science paper.

Confirmed: STAR Collaboration, 'Search for the chiral magnetic effect with isobar collisions at sqrt(s_NN)=200 GeV', Phys. Rev. C 105, 014901 (published 2022-01-03), the blind-analysis CME search on ~3.8 billion Ru+Ru/Zr+Zr collisions (2018 run) achieving 0.4% relative precision between the two systems — the same 2018 isobar dataset (~2x10^9 events per species) reused for the junction B/DeltaQ measurement. Follow-ups on the same data: PRC 110, 014905 (background baseline + CME upper limit) and PRR 6, L032005 (upper limit).

All three anchors confirmed as cited: (a) NA49, 'Baryon Stopping and Charged Particle Distributions in Central Pb+Pb Collisions at 158 GeV per Nucleon', Phys. Rev. Lett. 82, 2471 (published 1999-03-22) — net-proton spectra, net-baryon distributions derived. (b) BRAHMS, 'Nuclear stopping and rapidity loss in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(s_NN)=62.4 GeV', Phys. Lett. B 677, 267-271 (2009) — proton/antiproton spectra 0<y<3.1, rapidity loss 2.01+/-0.16 units (NOTE: PLB 677 is the 62.4 GeV paper; the 200 GeV BRAHMS stopping result is PRL 93, 102301 (2004)); HEPData record ins810481 exists. (c) STAR, 'Systematic measurements of identified particle spectra in pp, d+Au, and Au+Au collisions at the STAR detector', Phys. Rev. C 79, 034909 (2009) — pi/K/p/pbar dE/dx spectra at 62.4, 130, 200 GeV; part of the published net-proton yields used in the Science paper's measurement (c) exponential-scaling fit.

C.Y. Tsang et al. (4 authors; Tsang is BNL/STAR-adjacent), 'Beam energy dependence of net-hyperon yield and its implication on baryon transport mechanism', Phys. Lett. B 860, 139205 (Jan 2025), arXiv:2409.06492. Using published STAR Au+Au data: strangeness-corrected net-Lambda, net-Xi, net-Omega slopes are mutually consistent, consistent with net-proton, and centrality-independent — 'further substantiating the baryon junction picture'; PYTHIA valence-based implementations cannot simultaneously describe all baryons. Extends the junction case beyond protons to the full hyperon family.

entries.topic: (2) RECEPTION — strongest published alternative: CGC gluon saturation reproduces alpha_B WITHOUT junctions
entries.content: Oscar Garcia-Montero and Soeren Schlichting, 'Baryon stopping and charge deposition in heavy-ion collisions due to gluon saturation', Phys. Rev. C 111, 024912 (published 2025-02-21), arXiv:2409.06788. Within Color Glass Condensate EFT, charge is deposited via multiple scattering of VALENCE QUARKS off a saturated gluon target; their approximate analytic prediction of the baryon stopping parameter shows 'excellent agreement with experimental data extractions' from 62.4 to 5020 GeV (McDipper framework). This is a direct valence-quark-side counter-explanation of the alpha_B systematics — the exponential slope alone does not uniquely select junctions. (Conceptually descends from Itakura-Kovchegov-McLerran-Teaney NPA 730, 160 (2004), hep-ph/0305332 — the STAR paper's ref [35] — which already showed small-x valence evolution + saturation matches BRAHMS net-proton rapidity dependence and Regge theory.)

entries.topic: (2) RECEPTION — hydrodynamic charge-stopping baseline for the isobar observable
entries.content: Gregoire Pihan, Akihiko Monnai, Bjoern Schenke, Chun Shen, 'Unveiling Baryon Charge Carriers through Charge Stopping in Isobar Collisions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 182301 (2024), arXiv:2405.19439. (3+1)D relativistic hydrodynamics with multiple conserved-charge currents and charge-dependent lattice-QCD EoS, computing baryon and electric-charge deposition at midrapidity in Ru+Ru/Zr+Zr at 200 GeV explicitly 'to shed light on the existence of baryon junctions' — the quantitative no-junction baseline against which the STAR 1.84 value is to be judged.

Two 2025-2026 works push the neutron-skin-vs-junction disentangling the digest flags as a caveat: (a) Gregoire Pihan and Volodymyr Vovchenko, 'Disentangling baryon stopping and neutron skin effects in heavy-ion collisions', arXiv:2602.04079 (2026-02-03) — statistical-model analysis showing the excess baryon-stopping parameter gamma_B = (N_B/N_Q)(Z/A) can be quantitatively extracted from forthcoming RHIC charge/baryon-stopping ratios while CONTROLLING for nuclear structure; introduces an oxygen-baseline observable whose central-to-peripheral ratio is strongly sensitive to neutron-skin thickness; explicitly frames junction transport as one mechanism to be separated from skin effects. (b) Pihan, Monnai, Schenke, Shen, 'Neutron Skin from Conserved Charge Measurements at Collider Experiments', arXiv:2509.21644 — the inverse use: net-Q/net-B double ratios in p+Pb at 72 and 5020 GeV extract the Pb skin. Net reading: the community now treats the isobar B/DeltaQ observable as a JOINT probe of stopping mechanism + neutron skin, not a pure junction signal.

Mason Alexander Ross and Zi-Wei Lin, 'Baryon and electric charge stoppings in nuclear collisions and the role of strangeness', Eur. Phys. J. C 86, 143 (2026), arXiv:2510.22793. Shows in AMPT that the B/Q x Z/A ratio depends strongly on rapidity and is very sensitive to the s-sbar rapidity asymmetry: slightly more anti-strange quarks at midrapidity drives the ratio WELL BELOW one in Ru+Ru/Zr+Zr at 200 GeV — a mundane (junction-free) mechanism moving the observable, consistent with the Science paper's own note that AMPT sits even lower than UrQMD. A caution that the observable's baseline is model-sensitive through strangeness dynamics, cutting both directions.

Ting-Ting Duan, Fu-Hu Liu, Khusniddin K. Olimov, 'Valence quark-stopping and gluon junction-stopping scenarios in electron-nucleus collisions at the forthcoming Electron-Ion Collider: Which one is correct?', arXiv:2501.02819 (Jan 2025, v2 May 2025). Based on a multi-source thermal model analysis of soft+hard components of charged-particle distributions, the authors conclude experimental data 'indicate that the valence quark-stopping scenario is indeed accurate' and predict EIC e+A distributions to further validate it. This is the only located publication that flatly asserts the valence picture post-STAR; note it is a phenomenological thermal-model claim, not a microscopic calculation, and journal status is unconfirmed.

entries.content: Niseem Magdy, Prithwish Tribedy, Chun Yuen Tsang, Zhangbu Xu, 'Understanding baryon stopping at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider top energies', Phys. Rev. C (2025, new-style DOI 10.1103/ghb2-4y3s), arXiv:2504.09826. Uses PYTHIA-8 with advanced color-flow/color-reconnection (the CR Mode 2 machinery whose dynamically-formed junctions gave the 0.99+/-0.03 in the Science paper) to dissect which mechanisms of baryon transport 'mimic signatures of a baryon junction'. Author overlap with STAR (Tsang, Tribedy, Xu) — an in-house deepening rather than external criticism.

entries.topic: (2) THEORY post-2023 strengthening the junction side
entries.content: (a) D. Frenklakh, D. Kharzeev, W. Li, 'Signatures of baryon junctions in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering', Phys. Lett. B 853 (2024), arXiv:2312.15039 — local gauge invariance of the baryon wave function REQUIRES the junction; proposes JLab + EIC SIDIS tests. (b) Frenklakh, Kharzeev, Rossi, Veneziano, 'Baryon-number - flavor separation in the topological expansion of QCD', JHEP 07 (2024) 262 — Rossi and Veneziano themselves re-entering with Kharzeev. (c) Zohar Komargodski and Siwei Zhong, 'Baryon junction and string interactions', Phys. Rev. D 110, 056018 (2024), arXiv:2405.12005 — effective string theory of the junction: one new parameter (the junction MASS) controls the expansion; open-closed duality maps junction dynamics to closed-string vertices; perturbative-stability constraints on the junction mass. (d) 'The mass of the baryon junction: a lattice computation in 2+1 dimensions', JHEP 12 (2025) 019, arXiv:2508.00608 — first lattice determination of the junction mass parameter. Items (c)-(d) give the junction an independent, quantitative theoretical life beyond the Regge phenomenology.

Confirmed: D. Cebra, Z. Sweger, X. Dong, Y. Ji, S. R. Klein, 'Backward-angle (u-channel) production at an electron-ion collider', Phys. Rev. C 106, 015204 (2022), arXiv:2204.07915. Backward meson photoproduction: produced vector meson takes most of the struck-nucleon momentum, nucleon shifted several units of rapidity, |u| small / |t| large; 'shares a deep theoretical connection with the baryon-junction model'; projected omega rates 5M-100M events/year at EIC. Follow-on: 'Modeling backward-angle virtual Compton scattering at the future EIC', PRC 108, 055205 (2023).

Niseem Magdy, Abhay Deshpande, Roy Lacey et al., 'Search for baryon junctions in e+A collisions at the Electron Ion Collider', Eur. Phys. J. C 84, 1326 (2024), DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-13702-9, arXiv:2408.07131. Three proposed EIC measurements: (i) Regge intercept of net-baryon distributions in e+(p)Au; (ii) baryon vs charge transport in the e+Ru / e+Zr isobaric ratio (the isobar trick transplanted to DIS); (iii) target-flavor dependence of p/pbar yields at large rapidity from H and D targets in e+p(d). Community infrastructure: '1st Workshop on Baryon Dynamics from RHIC to EIC', CFNS Stony Brook, Jan 22-24 2024 (indico.cfnssbu.physics.sunysb.edu/event/113). Newest theory input: Spencer R. Klein, Mathias C. Labonte, Zachary Sweger, Gerald A. Miller, Ramona Vogt, 'Imaging baryon number density within the proton', arXiv:2603.03730 (Mar 2026) — from four exclusive backward meson-production channels in gamma-p, baryon number is confined to transverse radius 0.33-0.53 fm while charge/mass radii are >= 0.67 fm: baryon number is a COMPACT object inside the proton (junction-like), presented at RHIC/AGS users meeting (BNL indico).

entries.content: (a) Wendi Lv, Niseem Magdy, Rongrong Ma, Zebo Tang, Prithwish Tribedy, Chun Yuen Tsang, Zhangbu Xu, 'Measure charge transport in high-energy nuclear collisions with an energy scan of isobaric collisions', arXiv:2604.02825 (Apr 2026) — isobar beam-energy scan with the double-ratio technique to constrain conserved-charge transport mechanisms (the direct successor program to the Science measurement).
